content.title: About
content.content: Sugar‑free non‑chocolate candy are sweets made with sugar substitutes and flavorings, often featuring fruit or nut notes. They are suitable for people watching their sugar intake and for those who avoid chocolate for taste or dietary reasons.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sugar‑free candies often use stevia, erythritol or monk fruit as sweeteners.
The lack of chocolate makes them safe for individuals with cocoa allergies.
Some brands add natural berry extracts to boost flavor without added sugar.
Sugar substitutes typically do not cause a rapid spike in blood glucose.
These candies are frequently marketed as low‑carb or keto‑friendly.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Sugar substitutes do not raise blood sugar as sharply as regular sugar.

items.title: Supports diet plans
items.content: Suitable for low‑carb, keto, and weight‑loss programs.

items.title: Free of trans fats
items.content: Most non‑chocolate candies contain no trans fats when not made with hydrogenated oils.

items.title: Rich flavor with minimal calories
items.content: Flavorings and natural extracts provide a satisfying taste with a low calorie budget.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some varieties may contain nuts, dairy, or gluten.

items.title: Overconsumption of sugar substitutes
items.content: Large amounts of erythritol can cause mild gas or laxative effects.

items.title: Artificial sweetener content
items.content: Certain consumers prefer to avoid artificial sweeteners for personal reasons.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the candy as a standalone snack, mix into dessert blends, use in baking as a sugar‑free alternative, or as a garnish for dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the candy in a sealed container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For extended storage, refrigerate to maintain texture.
